newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real drops 0.06 pct in seesaw trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real drops 0.06 pct in seesaw trade.

text.p: Brazil's real dropped 0.06 percent to close at 1.0717 per dollar in seesaw trading on the commercial foreign exchange market, dealers said.
Players had speculated in the morning over possible strong dollar outflows, causing the real to drop 0.21 percent at 1.0734 per dollar.
But by the afternoon these large dollar outflows had apparently not taken place, allowing the local currency to recover some ground at the close, dealers added.
Preliminary figures for commercial and financial forex contracts showed a $65 million surplus on Wednesday.
Players were still waiting for a decline in the reais-dollar mini-band. The current mini-band was set by the Central Bank on Friday at between 1.0700 and 1.0750 reais per dollar.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real closed at 1.0756 per greenback, down 0.01 percent.
In the parallel market, the real fell 0.18 percent to end at 1.132 per dollar, traders said.
